newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Puts, cylinders traded in UK's FTSE index.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Puts, cylinders traded in UK's FTSE index.

text.p: Trading activity in UK equity options on Friday was dominated by deals in the FTSE 100 index, partly owing to expiry of the June contract this morning, dealers said.
Mixed trading also featured in the July series and a few call spreads executed for September expiry.

For July expiry, one large deal was to buy 500 July 4600 puts at 91p. Another was to sell 500 July 4500 puts at 49p. One trader established a long cylinder position by buying September futures at 4690 as well as selling 1,000 July 4900 calls and buying 1,000 July 4325 puts at net debit of 2p.

If the market rallies, profits will come from the long futures position until with the futures above 4900 the short calls may be assigned. Conversely, if the futures plummet below 4325, the losses can be cut by exercising the long puts.
Still with the FTSE, one of the bigger call spreads which was traded involved buying 630 September 4625 calls at 193p and selling 630 September 4875 calls at 70p for a net debit of 123p.
Maximum profit of 127p will be made if by September expiry, FTSE futures are above 4875.
By 1520 GMT, cash FTSE was down 53.7 to 4600.0 while September futures had tumbled 76 points to 4604.

In stock options, tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T Industries was busy in mixed trading. One of the larger deals was to sell 250 October 600 calls at 36p, another was to buy 275 July 600 calls at 18p.
Imperial Chemical Industries was also busy with a crossed trade involving 500 July 900 calls traded at 12-1/2p.
ICI shares fell 8-1/2p to 851p and B.A.T was up 5p to 587p.
